units.title: Smooth polynomial features in Gaussian L²
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. For every real polynomial \(p\) and every \(w\in E\), the literal function \(x\mapsto p(\langle w,x\rangle)\) belongs to \(L^2(\gamma_E)\). Its equivalence-class map is globally \(C^\infty\) on all of \(E\). The membership witnesses are produced by the proof and used to form these actual classes.
assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).
\(\gamma_E\) is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. No positive dimension restriction is imposed.
\(p\) has arbitrary real coefficients and arbitrary finite degree; \(w\) is any ambient vector.

steps.title: Build smooth powers in every finite integrability exponent
steps.text: Prove the power claim simultaneously for every finite \(q\ge1\). Constants give degree zero. Gaussian projection moments supply a linear map into \(L^{2q}\); finite-dimensionality makes it continuous and smooth. Multiply the lower power and the projection by the continuous Hölder bilinear map.
steps.lean:
private theorem smooth_power_ridge (n : ℕ) (q : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ q)] (hqtop : q ≠ ⊤) :
    ∃ F : E → Lp ℝ q (stdGaussian E), ContDiff ℝ (∞ : ℕ∞ω) F ∧
      ∀ w, (F w : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[stdGaussian E] fun x => ⟪w, x⟫_ℝ ^ n := by
  let μ := stdGaussian E
  induction n generalizing q with
  | zero =>
    have h : MemLp (fun _ : E => (1 : ℝ)) q μ := memLp_const _
    exact ⟨fun _ => h.toLp _, contDiff_const, fun w => by
      simpa only [pow_zero] using h.coeFn_toLp⟩
  | succ n ih =>
    have hq' : 1 ≤ 2 * q := (Fact.out : 1 ≤ q).trans (by rw [two_mul]; exact le_add_of_nonneg_right bot_le)
    have hq'top : 2 * q ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by norm_num) hqtop
    have : Fact (1 ≤ 2 * q) := ⟨hq'⟩
    have : ENNReal.HolderTriple (2 * q) (2 * q) q := ⟨by
      rw [ENNReal.mul_inv (.inl (by norm_num : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0))
        (.inl (by norm_num : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ⊤)), ← add_mul, ← two_mul,
        ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel (by norm_num : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0) (by norm_num), one_mul]⟩
    obtain ⟨F, hF, hFa⟩ := ih (2 * q) hq'top
    have hlin (w : E) : MemLp (fun x : E => ⟪w, x⟫_ℝ) (2 * q) μ :=
      IsGaussian.memLp_dual μ (innerSL ℝ w) (2 * q) hq'top
    let L : E →ₗ[ℝ] Lp ℝ (2 * q) μ :=
      { toFun := fun w => (hlin w).toLp _
        map_add' := by
          intro u v
          apply Lp.ext
          filter_upwards [(hlin (u + v)).coeFn_toLp, (hlin u).coeFn_toLp,
            (hlin v).coeFn_toLp, Lp.coeFn_add ((hlin u).toLp _) ((hlin v).toLp _)]
            with x huv hu hv hsum
          rw [huv, hsum, Pi.add_apply, hu, hv, inner_add_left]
        map_smul' := by
          intro c w
          apply Lp.ext
          filter_upwards [(hlin (c • w)).coeFn_toLp, (hlin w).coeFn_toLp,
            Lp.coeFn_smul c ((hlin w).toLp _)] with x hcw hw hsmul
          rw [RingHom.id_apply, hcw, hsmul, Pi.smul_apply, hw, real_inner_smul_left, smul_eq_mul] }
    let B := ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℝ
    let M := B.holderL μ (2 * q) (2 * q) q
    refine ⟨fun w => M (F w) (L w), ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact (M.contDiff.comp hF).clm_apply L.toContinuousLinearMap.contDiff
    · intro w
      change ⇑(B.holder q (F w) ((hlin w).toLp _)) =ᵐ[μ] _
      filter_upwards [B.coeFn_holder (r := q) (F w) ((hlin w).toLp _), hFa w, (hlin w).coeFn_toLp]
        with x hmul hf hl
      rw [hmul, hf, hl, pow_succ]

steps.title: Assemble the polynomial
steps.text: Polynomial induction builds the map using sums and scalar multiples of the smooth power maps. The almost-everywhere representative formulas are preserved at each step.
steps.lean:
induction p using Polynomial.induction_on' with
    | add p r hp hr =>
      obtain ⟨F, hF, hFa⟩ := hp
      obtain ⟨G, hG, hGa⟩ := hr
      refine ⟨fun w => F w + G w, hF.add hG, fun w => ?_⟩
      filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_add (F w) (G w), hFa w, hGa w] with x hsum hf hg
      simp only [hsum, Pi.add_apply, hf, hg, Polynomial.eval_add]
    | monomial n c =>
      obtain ⟨F, hF, hFa⟩ := smooth_power_ridge (E := E) n 2 (by norm_num)
      refine ⟨fun w => c • F w, hF.const_smul c, fun w => ?_⟩
      filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_smul c (F w), hFa w] with x hsmul hf
      simp only [hsmul, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hf, Polynomial.eval_monomial]
  obtain ⟨F, hF, hFa⟩ := representation
  let h : ∀ w : E, MemLp (fun x : E => p.eval ⟪w, x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E) :=
    fun w => (memLp_congr_ae (hFa w)).1 (Lp.memLp (F w))

steps.title: Identify the literal L² class
steps.text: The constructed map has the literal polynomial ridge as an almost-everywhere representative. Transfer square integrability along that equality and use extensionality of the quotient to identify the produced map with the stated class map.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨h, ?_⟩
  convert hF using 1
  funext w
  exact Lp.ext ((h w).coeFn_toLp.trans (hFa w).symm)

units.title: The actual Gaussian Hermite class
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. For each natural degree \(j\) and ambient vector \(w\), define the actual Gaussian \(L^2\) class of \(H_j(\langle w,\cdot\rangle)\). Here \(H_j\) is the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial. Its integer coefficients are mapped canonically to the reals, and the proved polynomial membership witness forms the quotient class.
assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).
\(\gamma_E\) is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. No positive dimension restriction is imposed.
\(j\in\mathbb N\) and \(w\in E\) are arbitrary. This defines a class; pointwise values of its chosen representative are not specified.

steps.title: Read the literal class construction
steps.text: The polynomial smoothness theorem supplies membership for the real image of \(H_j\). Apply its membership witness at \(w\) to form the actual class of the literal ridge.
steps.lean:
noncomputable def gaussianHermiteRidgeL2 (j : ℕ) (w : E) : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) :=
  let p := (hermite j).map (algebraMap ℤ ℝ)
  (Classical.choose
    (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialRidgeSmooth.standard_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_L2_smooth (E := E) p) w).toLp
      (fun x : E => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ)

units.title: Finite Gaussian Hermite feature sums
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. Let \(H_j\) be the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial and put \(h_j(w)=[x\mapsto H_j(\langle w,x\rangle)]\in L^2(\gamma_E)\). For a finite set \(S\subset\mathbb N\) and real coefficients \(c_j\), put \(F_{S,c}(w)=\sum_{j\in S}c_jh_j(w)\). This declaration defines the indicated finite sum in the actual Hilbert space. It imposes no unit-vector, parity, positivity or normalization condition.
assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).
\(\gamma_E\) is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. No positive dimension restriction is imposed.
\(S\) is any finite set of natural degrees, including the empty set. The coefficients are arbitrary real numbers.

steps.title: Read the finite linear combination
steps.text: Sum the constant scalar multiples of the degreewise classes in the same Gaussian Hilbert space. Empty support gives its zero element.
steps.lean:
noncomputable def finiteGaussianHermiteRidgeL2 (s : Finset ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ)
    (w : E) : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) :=
  ∑ j ∈ s, c j • gaussianHermiteRidgeL2 j w

units.title: Literal representatives of Hermite classes
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. Let \(H_j\) be the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial and put \(h_j(w)=[x\mapsto H_j(\langle w,x\rangle)]\in L^2(\gamma_E)\). For a finite set \(S\subset\mathbb N\) and real coefficients \(c_j\), put \(F_{S,c}(w)=\sum_{j\in S}c_jh_j(w)\). assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).

units.title: Global C² regularity of finite Hermite features
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. Let \(H_j\) be the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial and put \(h_j(w)=[x\mapsto H_j(\langle w,x\rangle)]\in L^2(\gamma_E)\). For a finite set \(S\subset\mathbb N\) and real coefficients \(c_j\), put \(F_{S,c}(w)=\sum_{j\in S}c_jh_j(w)\). Every finite feature map \(F_{S,c}\) is globally twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on the entire ambient space.
assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).
\(\gamma_E\) is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. No positive dimension restriction is imposed.
\(S\) is finite and \(c_j\) are arbitrary real coefficients. No unit-vector or series-convergence hypothesis is needed.

steps.text: Each degreewise map is \(C^2\). Constant scalar multiplication preserves that regularity, and the sum is finite.
